_comment: th#597 C5, RE-KEYED BY th#1987 (HARDCUT A9): THE tensorhub ref grammar conformance vectors. This file is vendored byte-identically in tensorhub (internal/orchestrator/release/testdata/) and python-gen-worker (tests/testdata/ + the wheel's gen_worker/contracts/); both parsers (Go ParseCanonicalRef, Python gen_worker.models.refs.parse_model_ref provider=tensorhub) must pass every vector. Grammar: owner/repo[@<release>|@sha256:<hex>|@blake3:<hex>][?<lane-spec>][#<cell-fragment>]. ONE `@` tail: it is a DIGEST when it reads <algo>:<hex> and the author-chosen RELEASE otherwise; a release is non-empty and carries no grammar separator (/@:#) — the catalog's ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]{0,63}$ CHECK is enforced where a release is CUT, not where a ref is parsed. One fragment token per ref, lowercased, charset [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,95}. THE FLAVOR SENSE OF `#` IS DELETED (th#2031 / pgw#1290): the fragment is the COMPILE CELL KEY of a platform cell repo `root/family-<f>` and NOTHING ELSE, so a `#` on any other repo is a REFUSAL vector and not a selector. It used to parse and then be dropped, resolving to whatever the release's default variant was with no error to see. The variant selector is the `?<lane-spec>` tail. THE `:tag` PRODUCTION IS DELETED: every `:` ref is a REFUSAL vector, and there is NO default and NO elision — a bare owner/repo names a repo and no artifact in it, which a hub resolve answers with the terminal release_not_found. 'canonical' is the NORMAL FORM the formatter must mint for the parsed value; format(parse(s)) == canonical and parse(canonical) == parse(s). th#2006 ADDED THE `?<lane-spec>` TAIL and with it two fields. It is cut AFTER the fragment split — a `?` on the FRAGMENT half is still the lockfile-attribution query both sides discard — and it is a RESOLUTION INPUT, never an address: it names WHICH variant of a release is meant, in the compact contract-pattern vocabulary endpointconfig.ParseCompact already reads, and it is not validated by the ref grammar. 'lane_spec' (default "") is the cut tail. 'address' is the SPEC-FREE wire form and defaults to 'canonical' when absent; it is what goes on the wire, into a residency key and into a binding row. The two minters differ BY DESIGN and the corpus names both: Go CanonicalRef.String() mints 'canonical' and CanonicalRef.Address().String() mints 'address', while Python's TensorhubRef.canonical() IS the address minter (the SDK must never mint a `?` onto the wire), so python asserts normalize_model_ref(ref) == address.
